key_insight: Mixing nanoscale Laponite with microscale Bentonite reduces drying damage, with most intermediate compositions on glass outperforming a simple average of the pure clays.
engineering_relevance: Clay composition offers a practical lever for improving drying resistance in coatings, barrier layers and ceramic processing.
method: Compare drying damage across clay compositions on hydrophobic polypropylene and hydrophilic glass.
Measure two-step yielding in gelled suspensions and derive step-dependent cohesive energies.
Relate peeling versus cracking to an energy-balance-derived cohesion–adhesion index.
evidence_signal: Replicate experiments found essentially intact Laponite films, extensive fracture in Bentonite films and two-step yielding across every composition.
watch_item: Rheology–cracking correlations must specify the yielding step because inferred cohesive energies differ by orders of magnitude; critical crack-free thickness remains unresolved.
paper_title: Resisting Drying Stress in Laponite Bentonite Clay Composites, Two Step Yielding and Crack Peel Selection
